result:
I've saved my best candidate to `final.py`. It scores **0.587** on the search split against the baseline's 0.365, and I used **16 of the 24 scorer calls**.

**How it works:** the cache runs 13 cheap "shadow" caches in the background, each using a different eviction policy. Each shadow gets a score that weights recent hits most heavily. The real cache copies whichever shadow is currently scoring best: it admits a new key only if that leader holds it, and evicts the leader's own victim first. It only switches to a different leader when that one is clearly ahead, which stops it flip-flopping. The 13 shadows are:
- **W-TinyLFU** (10 versions), varying how much space new keys get before they must prove they're popular (1% to 99% of capacity) and how fast old popularity counts fade.
- **ARC**, **S3-FIFO** and **LIRS**, three other well-known policies.

The point is that no single policy wins every kind of trace. W-TinyLFU on its own gets 0.50: it does well on loops but scores 0.60 on the "recency" trace, where LRU gets 0.85. Following the leader keeps the best behaviour on each trace:

| trace | final | W-TinyLFU alone | ARC alone |
|---|---|---|---|
| hot_with_scans | 0.251 | 0.247 | 0.240 |
| loop_and_hot | 0.670 | 0.656 | 0.299 |
| phases | 0.646 | 0.604 | 0.635 |
| mixed | 0.283 | 0.270 | 0.261 |
| recency | 0.847 | 0.597 | 0.847 |
| shifting_loops | 0.825 | 0.647 | 0.164 |

**Score progression:** ARC 0.407 → W-TinyLFU 0.503 → choosing among W-TinyLFU window sizes 0.541 → shadows of several policies 0.548 → several fading speeds 0.567 → switching only when clearly ahead 0.570 → adding S3-FIFO 0.571 → adding LIRS 0.587.

**Stopping point:** after that, nothing moved the score by more than 0.0003. Ideas that made no difference were more fading speeds, extra LIRS settings and an LFU-with-aging shadow. Two other combining ideas made results worse in my local tests:
- having all shadows vote on what to keep;
- smarter victim picking inside W-TinyLFU.

Extra S3-FIFO versions scored 0.5873 against 0.5870. I left them out because that gain is small enough to be noise and they add run time. In my local simulation the real cache ends up within about 0.01 of the best single shadow on every trace, so this approach has little left to give.

**Rules and run time:**
- One scorer call was wasted: a debug version used `getattr`, which the static check rejects. `final.py` passes the check.
- `final.py` takes about 1.7 s locally on synthetic traces the size of the real ones. The 8 s limit leaves room, but I couldn't see the scorer's own timing.
- Nothing is hard-coded to the traces. The shadows I dropped to save time are the ones that never led on my local traces, and dropping them didn't change the search score.

Everything is in `.../r14/nudge3/cache/`: `final.py`, my local simulator and the earlier versions in `work/`, and every scorer call logged in `calls.log`.
